one_liner: Twenty is an open-source CRM platform for managing people, companies, and opportunities, with a schema-generated REST/GraphQL API, offered both as a self-hostable open-source core and a paid cloud SaaS.

auth.notes: API key is sent as a static Bearer token; a separate OAuth flow exists for external apps acting on behalf of users, but grant types are not detailed on these pages.

evidence.snippet: For OAuth-based access (external apps acting on behalf of users), see OAuth

access.notes: The open-source core can be self-hosted for free, and an API key can be created immediately in Settings without payment or approval; Cloud also offers a 7-day no-card trial, but that is time-limited.

evidence.snippet: Self-hosting the open source core is free.
Pick 30 days (with card) or 7 days (without card). Both include full access — unlimited contacts, email integration, custom objects, API.
Create an API key in Settings → Developers → API → + Create key
REST and GraphQL APIs generated from your workspace schema.
There is no static API reference for Twenty.
Twenty sends an HTTP POST to your URL whenever a record is created, updated, or deleted.
Every Cloud workspace ships with a native MCP server. Connect your AI assistant via OAuth and it can read and write your CRM data in natural language.

buildability.rationale: Self-hosted deployment plus an instantly-created API key give free, working credentials against a documented REST/GraphQL API with webhooks and rate limits, and Composio already lists a 23-tool toolkit for it.

overview_evidence.snippet: Open-source core, self-hostable, export your data anytime.

unknown_reasons.auth: OAuth grant type details (e.g. authorization_code vs client_credentials) are not described on these pages, only that an OAuth flow exists for external apps.
unknown_reasons.api_surface: No OpenAPI/Swagger spec URL is published; API docs are generated per-workspace after creating an API key, so breadth is inferred from described CRUD + Metadata APIs rather than a fixed endpoint count.
unknown_reasons.mcp: The MCP server is described as shipping natively with Cloud workspaces, but no public MCP server URL or repo is given on these pages.
